removed: **Retention deadline** (ADR-0127, review of P/05 C4). Use the bucket's own persisted logical `written` from the event-journal contract “Bucket write time”. First resolve term reads and holds conservatively; a hold or unknown dependency keeps the bucket. For a closed, unheld bucket with readable `written`, delete exactly when `now >= written + seconds`: normal `<sub>` uses `seconds = retention.days * 86400`; `<sub>.alarms` uses `alarms_retention.days * 86400`; `audit`/`audit.alarms` use their journal term; `console`/`console.alarms` use their term with the longest-tree floor. A mirror copy uses the corresponding tree's term plus `MIRROR_RETENTION_EXTRA`, measured from its own copy `written`. Equality deletes; a time below the deadline keeps it. Neither window start/end nor filesystem `mtime` substitutes for `written`. Restore preserves the copy's `written`; it does not restart the retention clock. All usual conservative holds and read outcomes precede this predicate.
